dedupe_keys.name: urban tethys chloris ut c urban ecohydrological model

description: Urban Tethys-Chloris (UT&C) is a mechanistic urban ecohydrological model that couples ecohydrological land surface modelling with an urban canyon scheme, so the effects of ground vegetation, urban trees and green roofs on urban climate and hydrology can be simulated together. It covers the full urban energy and water balance, calculating 2 m air temperature, humidity and surface temperatures, and urban water fluxes including evapotranspiration, canopy interception, infiltration and soil moisture, while accounting for urban density, building properties and irrigation; the model description paper evaluated it against eddy-covariance measurements in Singapore, Melbourne and Phoenix. It was developed by Naika Meili, Simone Fatichi and co-authors and described in Geoscientific Model Development (2020); a 2025 release adds a building energy model (UT&C-BEM) for indoor cooling demand. The MATLAB code is available for download from Zenodo under CC BY 4.0, free of charge. Caveats: the model uses an infinite urban canyon approach, is written in MATLAB, and its hydrology excludes snow. It supports design of green-blue infrastructure for heat and runoff mitigation and climate adaptation studies of trees and green roofs; a related record is the global urban tree leaf area index dataset.
